KEY MESSAGE 1...Periods of unsettled weather are expected
through Friday.

Aloft, WSW'erly to WNW'erly cyclonic flow and embedded 
shortwave troughs affect our region through Friday as a longwave
trough axis moves from near the Upper Midwest and vicinity to
near the western Canadian Maritimes by sunset Friday evening. 
At the surface, a ridge continues to exit E'ward before a cold
front sweeps E'ward through Western and Central NY between
roughly midnight tonight and daybreak Thursday morning. Behind 
the front, a weak trough lingers over the eastern Great Lakes 
and vicinity, including our CWA, through Thursday. During 
Thursday night through Friday, a high pressure ridge should 
build gradually from the western Great Lakes and the axis of 
this ridge should become located near I-81 in our CWA by sunset 
Friday evening. Daytime heating and net low-level WAA in the 
warm sector will allow highs to reach mainly the mid 60's to 
lower 70's late this afternoon. Diurnal convective mixing of 
the boundary layer tapping into stronger flow aloft will 
continue to allow SW'erly surface winds to gust up to 30 to 40 
mph or so downwind of Lake Erie and up to mainly 20 to 30 mph 
elsewhere in our CWA through about 5 PM EDT this evening. 
Thereafter, surface gusts are expected to ease and then cease as
the boundary layer stabilizes via nocturnal cooling this 
evening. Cloud breaks and net low-level CAA behind the cold 
front will contribute to lows reaching the mid 40's to lower 
50's around daybreak Thursday. Net low-level CAA on the 
synoptic-scale will then persist through Friday. Late afternoon 
highs should reach mainly the mid 50's to mid 60's on Thursday 
and mainly the lower 50's to mid 60's on Friday amidst a 
primarily mainly clear to partly cloudy sky. In between, 
overnight lows should reach mainly the upper 30's to mid 40's 
around daybreak Friday.

Isolated to scattered rain showers and isolated thunderstorms
are expected along and ahead of the cold front as weak CAPE,
including elevated CAPE, is released by the following: moist
isentropic ascent preceding the axes of the aforementioned
shortwave troughs; low-level convergence/moist ascent along the
cold front and pre-front surface trough axes accompanying the
shortwave troughs aloft. Behind the cold front, primarily fair
weather is expected through sunset Friday evening. However,
periodic lake-effect rain showers should occur over/downwind of
Lake America amidst a W'erly to mainly WNW'erly mean low-level
flow of sufficiently-cold/moist air (e.g. 850 mb temperatures
near 2C to 4C) over/downwind of the ~17C lake and at least weak
lake-induced CAPE. These lake-effect rain showers should be
focused across Oswego County, the Tug Hill Plateau, and vicinity.
Isolated rain showers are possible late Thursday afternoon and 
early evening, especially across the Niagara Frontier, Finger 
Lakes, and North-Central NY, as weak potential instability in 
the lowest 1 km AGL is released by low-level convergence/moist 
ascent along surface trough axes attendant to shortwave troughs
aloft. Precip should end by sunset Friday evening, as the 
boundary layer stabilizes via nocturnal cooling and lake-induced
CAPE wanes via synoptic-scale low-level dry air advection and a
lowering subsidence inversion that will accompany the aforementioned
surface ridge. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Fair weather expected this Friday night through
Saturday.

Dry weather is expected this Friday night through Saturday as
the ridge at the surface and then aloft continues to build and
then crests E'ward across our CWA and vicinity, and is 
accompanied by stabilizing subsidence. Despite the development 
of weak net low-level WAA on the backside of the surface ridge 
Friday night, mainly clear sky, weak surface winds, and low 
humidity should allow overnight lows to reach mainly the upper 
30's to mid 40's around daybreak. Strengthening net low-level 
WAA and daytime heating should then allow late afternoon highs 
to reach mainly the upper 60's to mid 70's on Saturday, which 
are abnormally-warm for this time of year.

Note: weather pattern evolution at the surface and aloft may 
allow Tropical Cyclone Isaias' eventual remnant low to deliver a
widespread soaking rainfall to Western and Central NY this 
Saturday night through Sunday night. However, based on latest
trends in NWP model guidance, forecast confidence remains low 
regarding the evolution of multiple factors (e.g. the weather 
pattern aloft, the cyclone and its rain shield, and the track of
the surface low pressure center after landfall). Stay tuned to 
official forecast updates.
